Writing W1. First, checking what the turn record already supports, so the packet names real fields:㊥ (`"yes"`) W1 has gone to kimi-1 (job `invoke-1791184515290-32705-6be4555d`, park `park-96ef0ba7`, 60-minute deadline), and it's running. When it bells back I'll review and test it, load it into the live JVM, and watch one real work bell open a port and close it.

㊟ (one change from what I proposed) Leaving one item of a two-item request unreported won't keep that request open yet. That needs each acceptance item read as a separate act, and W1 is small enough without it. W1 treats a bell as one request, closed by the recipient's report. It does keep the request open if the job fails, is cancelled or times out. Reading the items separately can be W2. It fits with asking agents to mark their bells, because marked bells make the items easy to find.

㊢ (what W1 builds)
- **Opening:** a work bell between two registered agents writes a turn record, read classically with no 象 call. The caller is the requester and the recipient owes the answer.
- **Closing:** the completion attaches the recipient's reply, in the recipient's session.
- **What it needed changing:** the turn-acts adapter assumed every requester was you. For these records it now reads the requester's act from the bell's text.
- **Acceptance:** a replay of the claude-4 → codex-23 capture bell, taken from the real job ledger. There's a test showing that brief bells, auto-bellbacks and unregistered callers record nothing, and one planted bug per behaviour.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(the second cause) Emacs only sent a turn's reply to the JVM if 象 hadn't read the turn yet. Since 象 now reads when you send, a reply that takes longer than the reading was never sent. That's nearly every working turn, so since 03:08 today no reply text was stored, and no commits or ports either. claude-7's demo escaped because its replies were quick.
- **The fix:** Emacs now also sends the reply for turns already read. Turns with 象 switched off still never contact the JVM, which an existing test requires.
- **Checks:** a new test, plus a planted bug that it catches. Three older tests in `session-turn-analysis-dispatch-test` already fail without my change, and I haven't touched them.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(backfill)
- **Where the replies came from:** each record's reply was taken from the stored text (70), or found in the evidence store (68).
- **How it ran:** one record at a time, one second apart, through the same route Emacs uses. futon1b stayed healthy throughout.
- **Matching replies:** an agent's reply often doesn't point back at the operator turn it answers; its `in-reply-to` can be a tool step. So I matched the remaining replies by order within the session.
- **The 25 left over:** 23 of them have no operator evidence id, so there's nothing to look them up by.
- **What's still missing:** commits for the backfilled turns. The snapshot taken at the end of each turn is gone, so none of these turns will show a commit closing anything.
